messages.content: 尋找Netflix上《六人行》的電視節目列表及其評分，以及Hulu上《我們的辦公室》和《怪奇物語》的評分，並按照評分排序。

function.name: streaming_services_shows_list_and_ratings
function.description: Get a list of shows and their ratings on specific streaming services. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

streaming_service.description: Name of the streaming service. E.g., Netflix, Hulu, etc.

show_list.description: List of show names to search for on the platform.

sort_by_rating.description: If set to true, returns the list sorted by ratings. Defaults to false.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find Netflix list of "Six Feet Under" (六人行?) Actually "六人行" might be "Six Feet Under"? Wait "六人行" is Chinese title for "Six Feet Under"? Or maybe "Six Feet Under" is "六人行"? But the user says "尋找Netflix上《六人行》的電視節目列表及其評分，以及Hulu上《我們的辦公室》和《怪奇物語》的評分，並按照評分排序。" So they want:

- On Netflix: "六人行" (maybe "Six Feet Under") show list and ratings. They want the list of shows? Actually "六人行" is a single show. But maybe they want the list of episodes? But the function expects show_list: string[]. They want to get list of shows and ratings on specific streaming services. So we need to call function with streaming_service: "Netflix", show_list: ["六人行"], sort_by_rating: true.

- On Hulu: "我們的辦公室" (The Office) and "怪奇物語" (Stranger Things). So streaming_service: "Hulu", show_list: ["我們的辦公室", "怪奇物語"], sort_by_rating: true.

We need to call the function twice. The function returns any. We need to output the results. The user wants the list sorted by rating. So we should pass sort_by_rating: true.

Thus we will call the function twice.
